unseen_predictions.target: Dev mean R@1 of both_fresh against its matched both (stale) and none (queue-free) arms, batch 1024, ages 16 and 64, seeds 42/43/44
unseen_predictions.statement: both_fresh will recover most but not all of the queue-free score. I expect the fraction of damage attributable to staleness to be high (>0.7) but strictly below 1.0.
unseen_predictions.reasoning: The factorial showed harm beginning after a single optimizer step, which is the signature of staleness rather than of negative-set composition; but it also showed that conditions matched on measured drift differ in damage by up to 4.74pp, which means at least one non-staleness factor is active. A fraction strictly between 0.7 and 1.0 is the outcome consistent with both observations.
unseen_predictions.if_wrong: If the fraction is near 1.0, staleness is the whole mechanism and the matched-drift dissociation must be re-explained as a measurement artefact of path-length drift. If it is near 0.0, the harm is the extra negatives themselves - most plausibly unlabelled cross-image semantic false negatives - and the drift framing of the chapter is wrong, not merely incomplete.

unseen_predictions.statement: The residual damage that survives fresh re-projection will not grow with age.
unseen_predictions.reasoning: Whatever is left after staleness is removed should be a property of the negative set, whose composition does not depend on how long entries sat in the queue. Capacity does grow with age here, so a growing residual would instead indicate an entry-count effect.
unseen_predictions.if_wrong: A residual growing with age implicates queue capacity or false-negative accumulation rather than staleness, and would make the entry-count explanation primary.
